clue.text: Sportsman royal people detailed, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be put together some other way, rearranging them
read as de-tailed: the phrase loses its tail, its final letter

explanation.surface: Royals described in detail, perhaps alongside some sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' means docked of the tail, so ROYAL PEOPLE loses its last E; 'perhaps' then rearranges ROYALPEOPL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the mounted stick-and-ball game on horseback is a sportsman, one long associated with princes.

clue.text: It could turn out to be 1 ac's game

indicators.note: what the letters could turn out to be when rearranged

parts.note: the first word of the answer to 1 across names that sportsman's game

explanation.surface: A thing that might prove to be the game played by the earlier sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped '1' before 'ac's', which the scan shows: 1 across is POLO PLAYER, whose game rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pool is a cue game played on a table with pockets.

clue.text: One enjoys climbing them on board

definitions.text: One enjoys climbing them on board

parts.words: One enjoys climbing them on board
parts.note: not a sailor on a ship but a player of the children's board game with snakes, where some squares let a counter climb

explanation.definitionFit: In the board game with snakes, a player is glad to land on these and climb upward.

clue.text: Man with a message drops it casually around the unconverted

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on either side of the next piece
casually suggests the letters are thrown down in a careless new order

parts.note: a pagan is one not converted to the faith

explanation.surface: A preacher carelessly lets something fall among heathens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casually' signals the anagram and 'around' the container; the surface preacher dropping something hides that the unconverted are the heathen in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A propagandist spreads a political or religious message, so is a man with a message.

clue.text: Stole away and retired, clutching pipe

indicators.note: clutching means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night is abed
a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: Someone sneaked off and went to bed holding a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like having left work but means gone to bed, ABED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carried off by force is to be kidnapped, stolen away.

clue.text: Name remembered (in Devon, see) on Crispin's day

definitions.text: Name remembered (in Devon, see) on Crispin's day

parts.words: Name remembered (in Devon, see) on Crispin's day
parts.note: in Henry V's St Crispin's Day speech the king lists names to be remembered, one a duke; the same name is a Devon city and cathedral see

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry V says of Agincourt: 'Bedford and Exeter, Warwick and Talbot... be in their flowing cups freshly remember'd'. A see is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke so named is in Henry's Crispin's Day roll call, and the name is also Devon's county town and bishopric.

clue.text: Colour displayed during the cruise

indicators.note: the letters are on show running through the words the cruise

explanation.surface: Some shade of fabric shown off on a holiday voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow, the shade of unbleached linen, so a colour.

clue.text: Warning card

definitions.meaning: a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.definitionFit: A caution is an admonishment, and in old slang a caution is also a comical character, a card.

clue.text: Does this agent use an umbrella?

definitions.text: Does this agent use an umbrella?

parts.words: Does this agent use an umbrella?
parts.note: a spy working in secret, jokingly pictured as sheltering beneath a brolly

explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent works hidden, and someone sheltering beneath an umbrella is literally beneath cover.

clue.text: Immortal warrior?

parts.note: the song says veterans of the army never die, they only fade away, so such a fighter is deathless

explanation.definitionFit: The saying that veterans never die but simply fade away makes the long-serving fighter immortal.

clue.text: SW Asian cheese-maker, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard, giving a soundalike

parts.note: curd is what cheese is made from

explanation.surface: A dairyman from south-west Asia who produces cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Curd is pressed to make cheese, hence 'cheese-maker'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kurds are a people of south-west Asia, living across Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

clue.text: Pre-inflation drinks as stiffeners ?

parts.note: a farthing, a quarter of an old penny, was money from before prices rose
ales are drinks

explanation.surface: Cheap beers of the old days used as pick-me-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was a British coin worth a quarter of an old penny, withdrawn in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: Farthingales were hooped frames stiffening the skirts of Tudor dresses.

clue.text: French John turns tail in battle

indicators.note: the tail of the name, its last two letters, is turned round

parts.note: Jean is the French form of the name John

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named John flees from a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns tail' looks like running away, but it swaps the last two letters of JEAN, AN becoming NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Jena was the 1806 battle where Napoleon routed the Prussian army.

clue.text: The knight of the straw bat

definitions.text: The knight of the straw bat

parts.words: The knight of the straw bat
parts.note: the French word for a knight, and the surname of a famous French entertainer known for his straw boater hat

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for knight is also the name of Maurice, the singer whose trademark was a straw boater.

clue.text: Expedite punishments, say for fighters who got the wind up?

definitions.text: fighters who got the wind up?

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be heard and spelt differently

parts.note: to expedite is to hurry, and canes are punishments

explanation.surface: A call to speed up beatings for soldiers who were frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hawker Hurricane was an RAF fighter plane of the Second World War; 'got the wind up' means were scared, but here hints at storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawker's Hurricanes were fighter planes, and a hurricane is a great wind, hence the joke.

clue.text: LIke Samson, strong-not like the priest wakened at cockcrow

definitions.meaning: Samson kept his strength only while his hair and beard were never cut

definitions.text: not like the priest wakened at cockcrow
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme The House that Jack Built the cock that crowed in the morn waked the priest all shaven and shorn

explanation.definitionFit: Samson's strength lay in hair never cut, while the rhyme's priest woken by the cock was all shaven and shorn, so this is the opposite of him.

clue.text: Squadron-leader can go and get the beer

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: The RAF officer will go off and fetch the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squadron-leader' looks like the RAF rank, but it is just the first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old name for strong ale, so a kind of beer.

clue.text: Support for a heroic stand

parts.note: not backing for a brave defence but a base on which a hero's statue stands

explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base supporting a statue, typically of some hero.

clue.text: Like an old film, new version-dear me!

indicators.note: a new version of the words dear me is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A fresh version of a classic film provokes an exclamation of dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: An old film shot again is made a second time, as is often done with classics.

clue.text: With which Lothair took the floor?'

definitions.text: With which Lothair took the floor?

parts.words: With which Lothair took the floor?
parts.note: read Lothair as low hair: a tangled head of hair down at floor level, as on a cleaning implement

explanation.definitionFit: The head of a cleaning mop is used on the floor, and a shock of untidy hair is called the same.

clue.text: Descent from a tree

parts.note: not climbing down a trunk but lineage traced on a family tree

explanation.definitionFit: A recorded line of ancestry, as set out on a family tree, is one's descent.

clue.text: Angel painter

definitions.meaning: one of the archangels in the Book of Tobit
the Italian Renaissance artist of Urbino

explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is an archangel of scripture and the great High Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Very old flint, from a hole It could have made

indicators.note: the letters could have made something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A prehistoric flint tool, from a hole that it might have dug.
explanation.definitionFit: An eolith is a crudely chipped flint thought to be among the earliest human tools.

clue.text: South African brandy, suggesting a cigar?

definitions.meaning: a rough brandy once made in the Cape Colony
a cape is a headland, and a smoke is a cigar, so the name sounds like a cigar from the headland

explanation.definitionFit: Cape smoke was the nickname of a cheap brandy distilled in the Cape, and the second word sounds like something to puff on.

clue.text: College servants taking peins

definitions.meaning: at Cambridge and Durham a college servant is called a gyp
to give someone gyp is to cause them pain

explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge college servants are gyps, and gyp is also slang for pain, as in a knee giving one gyp.

clue.text: Turk with five in his harem?

indicators.note: in places the roman numeral inside the title

parts.note: a bey was a Turkish governor or nobleman
V is the roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A Turkish nobleman with five wives in his harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group, especially of women, a jokey picture of a harem.

clue.text: The boy who backed M Blum?

indicators.note: backed means the name is read from back to front

parts.note: Monsieur Blum is Leon Blum, the French prime minister of the 1930s

explanation.surface: A lad who gave his support to the French statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like support for Blum, but it reverses his first name, LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a boy's name, given especially to sons born at Christmas.

clue.text: Whisky perhaps is where the money is, in time

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
a till is where a shop keeps its money

explanation.surface: Asking where the cash is, in time, perhaps over a whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is an example of a spirit produced by distilling, a product of the still.

clue.text: It makes a splash

parts.note: not a dramatic success but the fizzy water added in a splash to a drink

explanation.definitionFit: A dash of fizzy water added to whisky is called a splash, so the mixer is what makes one.

clue.text: Drama in the kindergarten ? Easy !

definitions.meaning: a play performed by or for a young pupil
something so simple a youngster could do it

explanation.definitionFit: A nursery drama is a little one's play, and the idiom means something requiring no effort.
